method.what_this_is: A daily, source-linked briefing of two kinds of public health-tech signals: FDA clearances of AI-enabled medical devices, and private financings by health companies. Built for one reader (a non-technical founder tracking US health tech). Every record links to an official source. Facts come from those records. Analysis is written by a reviewer and labelled as interpretation. Nothing here is investment or legal advice.

evidence_classes.document_verified: FDA's 510(k) summary itself describes AI or machine learning. The summary may name the method (for example computer vision), which is recorded.
evidence_classes.manufacturer_reported: The manufacturer's own device or company name claims AI. Not checked against FDA documents.
evidence_classes.inferred: No document evidence. The FDA product code is AI-heavy, which is a guess.
evidence_classes.unknown: No evidence of AI either way.

dates.event_date: The underlying event: FDA decision date, or Form D first-sale date.
dates.filing_date: When the Form D was lodged with SEC (null for FDA records).
dates.signed_date: Date on the filer's signature (Form D).
dates.published_date: When the official source made it public, where the source says. Null when unknown.
dates.first_detected: The day this pipeline first saw the record.
dates.recency: new: event within 14 days of first detection. recent: 15 to 45 days. historical: older.

method.financing_categories: Derived from the Form D's own security-type flags, plus an EDGAR lookup. public-company private placement: the issuer has an exchange ticker in EDGAR. equity round, debt financing, mixed equity and debt, option-based or SAFE (SAFE only when the filer's note says so), other. An amendment (D/A) is an update to an offering, not a new raise.
known_gaps: Many digital health startups file Form D under Other Technology, so they are missed.
Form D asks for the amount sold to date. It does not say who invested or how the amount splits across securities.
Form D deadline checks adjust for weekends but not federal holidays, so a filing one business day over may be on time.
FDA's AI device list updates only every few months, so recent AI devices usually appear without that label.
A 510(k) summary with no AI language does not prove the device has no AI. It is ranked last, not deleted.
Only openFDA and SEC records are covered. There is no news, stock price or hiring data.
Analysis is written for a few records so far and is not independently reviewed.

stories.headline: Nanopath Inc reports $29.9M sold in a mixed equity and debt

analysis.author: Claude
analysis.why: The filing reports $29.9M sold of a $36.8M offering, tagged as both equity and debt, and it does not say how much was which. Calling it an equity raise would overstate what is known. It was filed 7 days after the 15-day deadline, which is a fact to note and not evidence of a problem. For a founder benchmarking round sizes, treat the number as total capital in a mixed offering, not as an equity valuation signal.
analysis.watch: Whether Nanopath announces the round with investors and the instrument split. A Form D names no investors; the four related persons listed are the company's own officers and directors.
basis: Form D 0001940981-26-000003: securities offered flagged as equity and debt; offering $36,760,740; sold $29,891,706; remaining $6,869,034; 21 investors.
First sale 2026-10-22 gives a 2026-11-06 deadline; the filing date from EDGAR's index is 2026-11-13; signature date 2026-11-10.

stories.headline: AngioInsight, Inc. reports $16.3M sold in a SAFE (per filer note)

analysis.author: Claude
analysis.why: This is a startup financing, not debt: the filing tags it as an option to acquire and the broker note describes the securities as SAFEs. It reports $16.3M sold to 94 investors, and the company says a placement agent (Cedar Point Capital) earned a 10% fee on the SAFEs it sold, which implies roughly $7.6M came through that broker (derived: $760,900 divided by 10%). The first sale was 2025-10-09 and the form was signed 2026-11-10, 382 days past the 15-day deadline, so this is a year of cumulative SAFE sales reported at once, not a new raise this week. Whether the lateness has any legal consequence is a question for counsel.
analysis.watch: Whether an amended Form D or a priced equity round follows, since SAFEs convert at the next priced round. The company's own announcements are the place to look; this pipeline does not track them.
basis: Form D 0002164579-26-000001: securities offered flagged only as option to acquire; offering $20,000,000; sold $16,314,000; 94 investors; commission $760,900 to Cedar Point Capital, LLC.
Filer note on the commission: '10% of the proceeds received from the sale of SAFEs by the Broker'.
First sale 2025-10-09 gives a 2025-10-24 deadline; signed and filed 2026-11-10.

stories.headline: Zai Lab Ltd reports $249.9M sold in a public-company private placement

analysis.author: Claude
analysis.why: Zai Lab has an exchange ticker (Nasdaq: ZLAB) and files 10-Qs, so this is a private placement by a public company, sold in full to 25 investors with a $7.5M placement fee to Leerink Partners (3.0% of the amount sold). It is not a startup financing and should not be used as a benchmark for early-stage rounds. It is more useful as a signal of how much capital institutional investors are putting into a listed biotech.
analysis.watch: Any 8-K or press release describing the terms and use of proceeds. This pipeline does not read those yet.
basis: EDGAR company record for CIK 1704292: ticker ZLAB, exchange Nasdaq, SIC 2834, large accelerated filer, 10-Q filed 2026-08-06.
Form D 0001704292-26-000038: $249,933,600 offered and sold, $0 remaining, 25 investors, commissions $7,498,008 to Leerink Partners LLC.
First sale 2026-10-27; filed 2026-11-09, inside the 15-day deadline.

analysis.author: Claude
analysis.why: FDA's own summary calls BlineSlide an AI-assisted tool but lists its algorithm methodology as computer vision, not machine learning, so 'AI device' needs that qualifier. It is a reading aid for lung ultrasound (absent pleural line motion), cleared against a fetal-ultrasound predicate (Sonio Suspect, K243614) under a product code FDA names for cancer-lesion diagnostic software. The summary also cites the company's earlier BlineSlide clearance (K252007, product code QIH). The applicant's address is London, CA with a Canadian-format postal code. For a founder, it is a worked example of clearing an ultrasound AI tool through a predicate from a different specialty, and of a Canadian company doing so.
analysis.watch: Whether FDA adds K261679 to its AI-enabled device list at the next update, and whether the summary's performance figures (standalone sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.87 on 818 cines; reader study aided AUC 0.922 vs 0.855 unaided) show up in the company's own claims.
basis: FDA record K261679: received 2026-05-21, decided 2026-10-23 (155 days), traditional 510(k), no predetermined change control plan authorized, product code POK (regulation 892.2060).

510(k) summary: indicated as a concurrent reading aid for lung ultrasound in adults; describes an AI-assisted tool; algorithm methodology listed as computer vision; predicate Sonio Suspect K243614 (machine learning based, fetal ultrasound); reference device BlineSlide K252007.
Applicant address on the FDA record: 45 King St., London, CA N6A1B8.
